title: PRD: Multi-Mode Lane Contracts, Scope Waterfall, and Launch Criteria for Hosted API
creator: Ava Gomez
description: High-level PRD for defining behavioral contracts, scope waterfall, and launch acceptance for multi-mode hosted endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). This ticket defines the contract matrix per lane, the gated evaluation and canary steps, rollback criteria, observability signals, and the final acceptance checklist for go/no-go. Intended to reduce ambiguity between product, eng, and design and to provide deterministic launch decisions for a phased rollout.
background: Customers are integrating multiple inference modes (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) via a single hosted API surface. Differences in behavioral expectations per lane, cost/latency profiles, and regional capacity have led to repeated scope creep at launch. We need a single source of truth that enumerates lane-specific guarantees, minimal viable behavioral contracts, and a staged rollout checklist to avoid rework and last-minute tradeoffs.
product_goals: Define lane-level behavioral contracts for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank
Provide a clear scope waterfall (MVP -> MVT -> Full) to control launch scope
Establish deterministic acceptance criteria and telemetry thresholds for canary and GA
Reduce customer-impacting regressions by tying eval suites to rollout gates
Document rollback and fallback policies that engineering can operationalize
out_of_scope: Major UX console changes unrelated to endpoint contracts
Dedicated capacity reservation mechanics (separate Dedicated product tickets)
Model architecture changes or model selection decisions — this PRD assumes model family compatibility
requirements: Lane contracts: short, machine-readable spec per lane describing determinism, max latency p95 target, tokenization/encoding expectations
Behavioral evals: a minimum set of diff tests for generation determinism and quality regressions per lane
Guardrails: default fallbacks and graded degradation policies when latency or quality SLOs are breached
Operational hooks: per-request trace identifiers, token-level cost estimates, and per-model rollout knobs
API compatibility: preserve existing request/response shapes for current customers; new lane flags opt-in
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: For each lane, a one-page behavioral contract exists that lists required output guarantees, non-deterministic allowances, and example failure modes
AC-2: Telemetry dashboard shows p50/p95 latency, error rate, and per-token cost for each lane and model variant over 48h test traffic
AC-3: Eval suite (automated) executes against the canary cohort and reports no >5% relative quality regressions on established prompt sets
AC-4: Canary deployment meets availability SLO >= 99.5% for 72 hours in a target region before expanding
AC-5: Rollback runbook is documented and can be executed in under 30 minutes by on-call engineer with documented postmortem template
AC-6: Console and API level feature flags exist to pin traffic to previous model variants and to opt lanes into graded degradation
AC-7: End-to-end security signoff completed for host-key, KMS usage, and access logs for private tenants
launch_checklist: 1) Finalize lane contracts and publish to the internal contract registry (link to artifact)
2) Bake evaluation fixtures for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank and attach to CI job map
3) Deploy canary to 2% of traffic in us-west-2 for 72 hours and monitor key telemetry
4) Run load tests that simulate mixed-lane traffic at projected 1x and 3x traffic profiles
5) Confirm cost reports and per-token billing is wired to billing pipeline and tested with synthetic tokens
6) Conduct runbook drill with on-call, SRE, and PM: simulate canary failure and perform rollback
7) Security checklist: KMS keys rotated, audit logs enabled, SSO/SCIM mapping validated for enterprise orgs
8) Conformance litmus: a small set of consumer SDKs hit the canary endpoints to validate API shapes
9) Communication: announce staged launch schedule and runbooks to Solutions/Support with TL;DR and rollback criteria
10) Post-launch evaluation plan: schedule 24h, 72h, 7d evaluation reports and a 30-day quality review
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Internal Canary: engineering + QA traffic only, validate instrumentation and rollback (48h)
Phase 1 - External Canary: 2% external traffic, run automated evals per lane, verify SLOs (72h)
Phase 2 - Gradual Ramp: increase to 20% over 3 days while monitoring cost and quality signals
Phase 3 - Regional Expansion: open additional regions (eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1) with capacity checks
Phase 4 - GA: full lift with announcement, enable payer-tiered SLAs and billing
telemetry_and_slas: Minimum telemetry: request id, lane tag, model_id, tokens_in/out, latency_ms, error_code
SLOs per lane: chat p95 latency <= 450ms (hosted-optimized models), completion p95 <= 300ms, embeddings p95 <= 120ms, rerank p95 <= 350ms
Quality SLO: automated evals must not regress more than 5% relative to baseline on guarded prompt sets
Alerting: page when error rate >1% sustained for 10 minutes or latency p95 breaches target by 30% for 15 minutes
Reporting cadence: 24h canary summary, 72h deeper analysis, 30-day quality report with customer-impact notes
dependencies: ENG-48210: Runtime batching and lane tagging support
ENG-49876: Per-request token accounting and billing export
ENG-50123: Canary routing and rollout service enhancements
PM-208441: Billing validation for per-token invoices (billing team signoff)
DES-1335: Minimal response schema and example fixtures for lane contracts
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Eval suites are not representative of customer prompts -> Mitigation: recruit 3 early adopters for a shadow test and expand prompt sets
Risk: Regional capacity shortages during ramp -> Mitigation: pre-book burst nodes on Dedicated for critical regions and enable cross-region fallback
Risk: Unexpected cost blowouts from batching inefficiencies -> Mitigation: enforce per-model cost guardrails in the console and disable heavy batching for early traffic
post_launch_actions: Ship 24h canary report to execs and correlate regressions with customer-facing tickets
Schedule 30-day quality review and iterate on lane contracts based on observed failure modes
Roll out documented lessons learned into the contract template and PRD checklist
